quotes.text: If there's one idea to hold on to for the full episode, it's this. Autonomy fails at boundaries, not capabilities.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central thesis in one line.

quotes.text: Copilot optimizes an individual. Autonomy optimizes a queue. Copilot makes one person faster at doing work. Autonomy makes work happen without that person being involved.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a clear, memorable line between assistance and autonomy.

quotes.text: Autonomy doesn't create new governance problems. It simply turns your existing governance gaps into runtime behavior.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why governance gaps become live risk once agents can act.

quotes.text: MCP makes tool discovery easy. It does not make authorization safe. Discovery is not authorization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A precise warning about treating tool registries as permission systems.

quotes.text: If you can't name who wakes up at 2am when the agent fails, you're not ready for autonomy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple readiness test for any autonomy initiative.

chapters.title: What Altera represents in Microsoft terms
The autonomy stack and control plane versus execution plane
Scenarios: IT remediation, finance reconciliation and security triage
Identity debt, authorization sprawl and MCP

takeaways: Copilot speeds up a human, while autonomy replaces the human step, so the real design work is the autonomy boundary and the execution contract that governs what an agent may do.

Governance lives in the control plane, with Entra identities, least privilege, tool allow lists, evidence rules and real kill switches, not in the agent's prompt; MCP makes tool access easy but not safe.
Autonomy is worth it only for repeatable, well-instrumented work with clear owners, and should be measured by cost per outcome, time to close, human-in-the-loop rate, rollbacks and policy violations.
hook: Most organizations still treat Copilot as a smarter chat box, but autonomous agents that act on Graph, Azure, Defender and Entra turn every sloppy permission into live risk. This episode is for enterprise architects, IT leaders and Microsoft 365 platform owners who need to define the autonomy boundary, execution contracts, identity controls and evidence trails before autonomy reaches production.
